verdict.root_cause: At 06:52:47-06:52:48 the platform-automation pipeline moved every hotel-reservation mongod container from mongo:4.4.6 to mongo:8.0.14-rc0, a multi-major jump onto a pre-release build, as the last change before onset [tr_73ec19bd8628][tr_2cae39058274][tr_baad9dab95a5]. The new binary cannot complete startup: each mongod logs an orderly, self-initiated shutdown from the initandlisten thread with exit code 62 (mongod's version/on-disk-format incompatibility abort) at 06:53:47 (rate), 06:53:49 (geo) and 06:53:53 (user) [tr_56d7f7ea455d][tr_b6ac44351d92][tr_bcb3a8416cae]. The processes never reach a listening state, so all five mongodb services alert together at 06:53:54 as their pods crash-loop. The running artifact is not one that can start here; the fix is to restore the 4.4.6 image.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent change queries show the same act on three different instances: same actor, same ~47-second burst, same 4.4.6 -> 8.0.14-rc0 image move last in sequence [tr_73ec19bd8628][tr_2cae39058274][tr_baad9dab95a5]. That explains five simultaneous alerts from a seed the graph does not connect - they share a rollout, not a call path. Three independent log queries show the same symptom: exit code 62 in the initandlisten context with a complete sub-20ms shutdownTask and a clean WiredTiger close [tr_56d7f7ea455d][tr_b6ac44351d92][tr_bcb3a8416cae]. The process exits under its own control before accepting any client, which closes OOM/SIGKILL, load saturation, hangs and graceful orchestrator stops; the clean storage-engine close and successful fs-lock removal argue against an unreadable or full store. What remains is a binary that refuses to run against what it finds. Both metrics dispatches failed structurally - these services emit no span-derived metrics [tr_d1c94edb180d][tr_af3c6cb81e1c] - so no resource curve was available either way.
open_questions: The triggering assertion line before each shutdown was never retrieved; all three log results are truncated to the shutdown tail [tr_b6ac44351d92][tr_bcb3a8416cae][tr_56d7f7ea455d], so exit 62's meaning rests on convention, not this environment's own error text.

Why freshly created PVCs would carry data the 8.0 binary rejects - recommendation-pvc was created at 06:52:00 inside the same burst [tr_baad9dab95a5], explicitly ruling out a reused 4.4-era volume there.
mongodb-profile was never dispatched against; its participation is inferred from the other four, and the failure-admin-geo ConfigMap mounted at /scripts on geo only [tr_73ec19bd8628] was never read.

alternatives.root_cause: The mongodb volumes hold content the binary cannot decode on read, aborting startup.
alternatives.why_not: WiredTiger opened and closed cleanly on all three instances with successful rollback-to-stable and checkpoint and no storage errors [tr_b6ac44351d92][tr_bcb3a8416cae][tr_56d7f7ea455d]; the abort appeared only after the image moved, pointing at the artifact rather than the contents.

alternatives.root_cause: The failure-admin-geo ConfigMap mounted at /scripts supplies a startup directive that makes mongod abort.
alternatives.why_not: That mount is reported only for mongodb-geo [tr_73ec19bd8628], yet rate and user show the identical exit-62 startup abort [tr_56d7f7ea455d][tr_bcb3a8416cae]; the only change common to all three is the image.

proposal.expected_effect: After redeploying mongodb-geo at mongo:4.4.6 (the tag recorded immediately before the 06:52:47 platform-automation image update), the recreated mongod should complete startup instead of aborting: the Loki stream for {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-..."} should stop emitting the initandlisten 'Shutting down' record with exitCode 62 and should instead reach a 'Waiting for connections' / listening line, and the pod's restart count should stop incrementing. The mongodb-geo alert that fired at 06:53:54 should clear. Note that mongodb-geo emits no span-derived metrics [tr_d1c94edb180d], so error-ratio/latency panels cannot confirm this — confirmation must come from the pod log tail and restart count, not Prometheus.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, on 4.4.6, mongod still logs an initandlisten shutdown with exitCode 62 (or any non-zero startup abort) and the pod keeps crash-looping past the confirmation window — that would mean the abort is driven by something other than the binary version, e.g. the failure-admin-geo ConfigMap mounted at /scripts at 06:52:04 [tr_73ec19bd8628], which was never read, or by PVC content/permissions. Also falsified if the process starts but no caller traffic recovers, which would put the fault downstream of the database. The triggering assertion line before each shutdown was never retrieved, so exit 62's meaning here rests on convention rather than this environment's own error text; that is the main weakness in this proposal.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this costs a container recreate on an already-dead service and, worse, buries the real trigger: re-pinning to 4.4.6 may make geo start while leaving a mounted fault-injection artifact (/scripts, failure-admin-geo) in place and unexamined, so the same failure can recur on the next pipeline run. If any 8.0-rc data had been written to geo-pvc, a 4.4.6 binary would itself refuse those files — the logs show a clean WiredTiger close with rollback-to-stable and no listening state reached, so this is unlikely but not excluded, and the failure mode would be an identical crash-loop at the older tag. This also diverges geo's image from the four sibling mongodb instances still on 8.0.14-rc0, leaving the deployment inconsistent until they are handled the same way.
proposal.blast_radius: One service. mongodb-geo's inbound callers in the hotel-reservation dependency graph see the connection reset while the container is recreated — but those callers are already failing, since mongod has not been reachable since 06:53:49 [tr_b6ac44351d92], so the marginal impact is near zero. This does not touch mongodb-rate, mongodb-user, mongodb-recommendation or mongodb-profile, which remain crash-looping on the same image and will each need their own decision; mongodb-profile in particular was never directly observed and its participation is inferred.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Five distinct MongoDB instances alerting simultaneously at the same second points to a shared substrate problem (host, storage, or config rollout) rather than per-service noise. Warning severity alone doesn't justify dismissing a synchronized datastore-tier event.
